summary: Backpressure snowball causing elevated 5xx floor during mixed embedding + streaming workload
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC BrightTask started seeing persistent 5xx responses (502/503) on chat + embedding mixed routes. Error rate rose from ~0.5% baseline to 8-12% within 15 minutes and did not self-resolve. Impact: Multiple customer endpoints experienced degraded availability; retries amplified traffic and prolonged the incident. Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant brighttask-dedicated-4) in us-east-1, serving runtime v2.7.1, api-gateway v1.12. Steps to reproduce: 1) Reproduce test by issuing a tight loop of 50 concurrent streaming chat requests while simultaneously uploading a 10k line embedding batch. 2) Observe increasing apigw queue length and subsequent 502/503 responses. Observed behavior: api-gateway latency climbs, keepalive pool saturates, apigw threads spend >90% time waiting on upstream responses. Upstream runtimes enter crash/restart cycles with OOM-like logs and watchdog restarts. Expected behavior: graceful shedding or FIFO backpressure and fallbacks without sustained 5xx floor. Logs/metrics: apigw 502/503 spikes starting 11:22 UTC, runtime restarts per instance increased from 0.02/hr to 1.6/hr. KV cache eviction rate spiked coincidentally. Customer impact: BrightTask reported user-facing errors for ~40 minutes. Temporary workaround requested.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:35 UTC - Support (Aisha): Escalated to SRE. Gathering logs and tenant routing info; asking customer to pause bulk embedding uploads if possible.

2026-03-12 11:42 UTC - SRE (Liam): Observed apigw accept queue length jump and keepalive pool saturation. Pinpointing origin to mixed embedding upload + long-lived streaming sessions from same tenant. Obtained heap profiles from runtime nodes: showing KV cache thrash and increased GC pauses.

2026-03-12 12:03 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms they throttled embedding uploads; error rate dropped to ~4% but runtime restarts continue. Customer provided correlation IDs and request IDs for 11:22-11:40 UTC.

2026-03-12 12:28 UTC - SRE (Liam): Applied emergency mitigation: enabled route-level concurrency limit for BrightTask streaming routes and temporarily raised HPA min replicas for their dedicated pool. Observing stabilization but still elevated tail latency.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Eng (Marta): Identified a kernel selection regression in v2.7.1 when sequence lengths vary widely; leads to increased memory working set and delayed KV cache evictions under mixed workloads. Drafting a patch.

2026-03-14 08:50 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of planned fix rollout window and recommended permanent configuration changes (separate routes for bulk embedding uploads and streaming chats, plus client-side jitter/retry backoff).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Mixed workload (large embedding uploads concurrent with streaming) causes apigw connection saturation leading to hedged retries and retry amplification.

Hypothesis 2: Serving runtime kernel selection regression in v2.7.1 increases memory pressure when model variants with different sequence-length profiles are hot-swapped, causing frequent GC and runtime restarts.

Evidence: Correlation between KV cache eviction spikes and runtime OOM-like restarts; heap profiles show memory spikes when embedding shard compaction runs concurrently with streaming KV cache accesses.
Temporary mitigation validated: route-level concurrency cap reduced 502 rate by ~65% within 10 minutes; HPA bump reduced runtime restart frequency by ~70%.

Planned permanent fix: patch kernel-selection heuristics + add early backpressure signal from runtime to apigw for long-lived streaming sessions. Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4382
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround applied: route-level concurrency limit for tenant streaming routes and raised HPA min replicas to smooth capacity. Engineering to ship kernel-selection patch in runtime v2.7.2; will also add a configuration guide recommending separate ingestion endpoints for bulk embedding uploads to avoid mixed-workload amplification. Follow-up: schedule tenant-specific postmortem and update backpressure runbook. Customer asked for proactive alerting on future sustained 5xx >3% for 15m.
